newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BIL says Thistle price set to ensure good float.
newsitem.headline: BIL says Thistle price set to ensure good float.

text.p: A spokesman for New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd said on Wednesday its float of Britain's Thistle Hotels had been priced at the bottom end of the range to ensure a strong book and a solid share register.
Spokesman Mike Drogemuller said most of the top British institutions had supported the offer and BIL considered it more important to get a good register.
"That reflects the lower price," he said. "It's important that the float gets away positively."
Brierley earlier announced the Thistle offer price had been set at 170 pence per share, at the bottom of the indicative range of 170 to 210 pence.
BIL still held 80 percent of its stake in Thistle and it would await developments in the secondary market, Drogemuller said.

Under the terms of the issue, BIL and the other major shareholder, the government of Singapore which held 30 percent of Thistle before the float, are required to retain their remaining holdings for 12 months.
Drogemuller said the slide in the BIL share price from a recent high of $1.44 indicated that the market had accepted the Thistle price would be at the bottom of the indicative range.
"We have a quality book on the Thistle register so from that point of view we are quite happy and hopefully it will be a good story further out," he said.
At 2230 GMT, after an hour's trade, Brierley Investments was down two cents at $1.37 on volume of 351,677 shares.
